assign.request: Can a USD 10/month membership fund cent-scale tipping and payouts without becoming a payment processor?

log.msg: gotcha: double-quoted --title/--summary in bash let $0/$1/$2/$10 etc expand as shell positional params, silently eating every dollar amount (entry.mjs help text warns exactly this - missed it); wiped ~39 corrupted entries back to the seed line and rewrote everything single-quoted

50-entry log.jsonl (0 torn, 0 refused) + verdict.md landed: no stored-value/tipping-balance on day one, Stripe Billing membership only, defer tipping to a real per-tip Connect charge or a pooled payout

assign.outcome: **No stored-value tipping balance on day one.** Ship the $10/month membership on Stripe Billing (Payment Element + Customer Portal) — about $0.66/subscriber/month (6.6%). Do not build any spendable, sendable tipping balance: Stripe enforces a $0.50 minimum charge (a real 1-cent tip is impossible), and a balance sent between users reads as money transmission, not a closed-loop gift card — FinCEN's own closed-loop exemption is redemption-with-a-merchant, not peer-to-peer transfer. Defer tipping to a real per-tip Stripe Connect charge above $1, or a Flattr/Medium-style periodic pooled payout — both clear the fee floor without the platform ever holding a balance. See the [verdict](/imagine/platform/research/payments/verdict/) and the [50-entry log](/imagine/platform/research/payments/) (0 torn, 0 refused; 31 established / 8 contested / 11 speculation across 32 findings, 13 opinions, 4 questions, 1 theory). Open item: whether a non-cashable balance that only multiplies a real, simultaneous Stripe charge escapes stored-value rules — needs paid counsel, not more search. Also fixed and logged: an early batch of ~39 entries got silently corrupted by double-quoted bash args letting $0/$1/$2/$10 expand as shell positional params — wiped and rewrote all of them single-quoted before the final --check passed clean.
